commits.summary: Symbolic references in the own checker: paths that differ only in a reference merge, the reference a guarded choice of objects (H1, verification pending)
commits.body:
The own checker (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs) represented every reference as a known object index or null, so paths that met with a reference to different objects never merged. A reference may now be a Choice: one of the path's objects or null, each under a guard, the guards exclusive and covering the path's condition. It is made where such paths merge, and by a field read through one. if_acmp, ifnull, ifnonnull and instanceof on a choice are formulas over the guards; getfield chooses among the candidates' fields, and putfield writes each candidate's field under its guard, with NullPointerException where the reference is null. Every other use that needs the object (a call's receiver, a JDK call's argument, an array instruction, checkcast, athrow, a monitor) splits the path per candidate first, as an index into an array of references already did. A known reference stays the fast path and never becomes a formula.

Verified inline: a new test, lib/tests/heap.rs, checks three Java claims merged from the start and never merged, with the same verdicts both ways, and every violation's witness fails the claim on a real JVM. Ten independent choices between two objects and a write through the chosen one take 22 paths merged and 1024 unmerged. Three new conformance cases (swaps, swapsOrNull, swapsThenNull), past the 512-path merge threshold, agree with the JVM. The unit tests (183), integration.rs (64), conformance.rs and foundations.rs pass, and the aliasing cases keep their verdicts. lib/benchmark/conformance.json was regenerated for the three cases.

Job 20261107-041414 runs the benchmark on the own checker and compares every run with lib/benchmark/results.json. Expected: no verdict changed, no formula grown past 10%, and paths or merges changed only in the new cases. It is listed for review in llm-dlc/loops/foundations-heap.md, which records H1 as done pending that job, with H2 next.

commits.summary: Array parameters that may be null or one array in property checks, decided by the own checker with witnesses that keep identity (H2, first step; verification pending)
commits.body:
jvmcontract prove takes --nullable a and --may-alias a,b for array parameters (step H2 of llm-dlc/loops/foundations-heap.md, its first targets the conformance corpus's inputs outside the domain). The own checker makes each such parameter a symbolic reference (H1's Choice) among null, its own array and the own arrays of the parameters before it in its group (bmc::Parameters), and reads back from a model which one it holds (raw_same, a new Argument::Same). The domain line and the statement say what the domain is ('a: int[] of length ≤ 8, or null', 'a and b may be the same array'); --engine jbmc and --confirm refuse it since JBMC would prove a narrower claim, and auto doesn't fall back to JBMC. The expression language gained a == null and a == b over array parameters. Witnesses keep identity everywhere: the interpreter, the shrinker and the JVM run (jvm_witness.rs now passes null and one array twice) never split or join arrays, and a witness reads twoArrays(a=[0], b=the same array as a). The harness's \old copy of a null array is null.

Verified inline: six new conformance claims over widened domains (twoArrays under --may-alias, length and lengthOrMinusOne under --nullable), each Verified or refuted as the JVM decides, their witnesses refuted on the JVM; default-domain claims unchanged; new unit tests for the engine's choices merged and unmerged, and a JVM run with one array twice and with null (lib/tests/heap.rs). Unit tests (185), integration.rs, conformance.rs, foundations.rs and heap.rs pass; one integration test failed once under the other streams' load and passed alone.

Job 20261107-043420 (for review): the corpus's ignored JBMC, auto and auto --confirm runs, expected to pass with the widened claims refused under JBMC and --confirm.

commits.summary: Objects made by their constructor as regression inputs, compared on their fields as both versions leave them (H2, second step)
commits.body:
A regression check now takes a parameter of an application class: the harness makes it by the class's one usable constructor from symbolic arguments, an object argument made by its own constructor in turn (Line(Money price, int quantity) of a Money(long cents)), its primitive leaves the harness's parameters by path (l.price.cents). Both versions get their own objects from the same leaves, the old one's under before/, and after the calls their fields are compared, followed into the objects they refer to. The domain says the claim covers only objects made by that constructor from arguments it accepts, so a difference only in a state the constructor never makes is outside it; the statement lists the observed field paths; a witness is a construction recipe, new Line(new Money(0), 1), and the replay shows what each version left in the object. Classes outside this (a superclass, several constructors, a String field or argument, a class reaching itself, different shapes in the two versions) are refused naming why. Identity, nullability and aliasing among objects, results of such classes and property checks over them come next. Done in regression checks before property checks, against the brief's Progress note of last step, because the integration contract's heap part is regression checks.

Verified inline: lib/tests/heap.rs adds five checks on the own checker (a rewrite verified with the domain words, a changed result and a change seen only in the object as left both refuted with recipe witnesses, a difference only where the constructor rejects verified with the domain saying so, a String field refused). Unit tests (185), heap.rs (9), integration.rs (64, on a rerun; one test failed once under the other streams' load), conformance.rs and foundations.rs pass. No job.

commits.summary: Results of classes made by their constructor compared by their fields, and identity relations within each version compared as holds-before-iff-holds-now (H3, first step)
commits.body:
Regression checks now compare a result of an application class (other than a record of primitive components) field by field, as object parameters are, where it was compared by Objects.equals, which across the two versions' distinct classes is identity. They also observe identity within each version: the result, array parameters, object parameters made by their constructor and the object or array fields those reach, every two of one static type under the same path in both versions compared as 'holds before iff it holds now' (result == l, result.price == l.price), never by comparing objects across versions. The statement lists them (observations.identities) and each replay states which relations hold, so the alias-to-copy defect (a copy with the same values handed back in place of the argument) is refuted with a witness whose two replays differ only there; an array filled in place and then copied likewise.

Verified inline: four new checks in lib/tests/heap.rs on the own checker (an alias handed back verified; the alias-to-copy defect refuted; a Line result compared by fields, a rewrite verified and a changed quantity refuted; an array copied refuted by result == a), and the unit (185), heap (13), conformance, foundations and integration suites pass. One integration test timed out under the other streams' load in a 615 s run, as in the two earlier steps, and passed alone in 11.6 s. Next per the brief's Progress: H5's narrow case and spec::heap::check on the joint example.
